item.title: Outmarket in California AI Raises $34.5M Series B
item.description: San Francisco-based Outmarket AI announced it has raised $34.5 million in Series B funding. The funding comes months after the company announced a $17 million Series A. The latest round brings Outmarket’s total funding to $56.5 million.

item.title: AI Safety Measures Widely Backed by Most Americans, Poll Finds
item.description: A vast majority of Americans favor requiring artificial intelligence companies to meet independent safety benchmarks for their models, even if those standards mean slowing development of the technology, according to a new poll. to establish guardrails for AI systems, with 81% indicating that safety should come before the pursuit of innovation, according to the poll released Wednesday by Quinnipiac University. In lieu of new federal rules, the executives agreed to voluntary measures that include third-party safety assessments of models and more stringent internal controls over their systems.

item.title: Nuclear Startup Funding Is Up, But The Sector’s Public Markets Take A Bearish Turn
item.description: For a bigger-picture view, below we charted 11 of the largest funding rounds for the nuclear sector this year. Funding to nuclear power-focused startups hit an all-time high this year, fueled by expectations of surging energy demand around artificial intelligence. Much of this year’s funding went to a few heavily financed nuclear startups.

item.title: The IPO Window Is Opening Selectively; Readiness Will Decide Who Gets Through
item.description: Public-market activity is returning selectively, led by companies that used the slower years to build scale and strengthen their financial and operating foundations. Collectively, venture-backed startups raised $110.8 billion through IPOs, compared with $12.6 billion a year earlier. For founders, late-stage startups and investors tracking exit readiness, the message is not simply to wait for a better market.

item.title: Generali’s aggregate reinsurance in focus as European cats and weather bite in 2026
item.description: Analysts at investment bank Jefferies have brought insurer Generali’s aggregate reinsurance protection into focus, saying that losses from catastrophes and weather events in Europe could drive the insurer to make reinsurance recoveries from its aggregate protection this year, given the restructuring of the coverage for 2026. Generali had restructured its aggregate reinsurance arrangement for the 2026 calendar year, to provide greater protection against frequency loss events. The Jefferies analyst team came away from its meeting with Generali’s management saying, given the loss run-rate in Europe from weather and catastrophes this year, “It seems likely that Generali will hit the aggregate reinsurance retention (unlike last year).”

item.title: Catastrophe bond market keeps record pace after above-average Q3: Report
item.description: Catastrophe bond issuance was above-average at $948 million for the third-quarter of the year which has served to keep the market on pace to set new records, with total nine-month 2026 issuance reaching a new $18.9 billion high of risk capital analysed and tracked by Artemis, our latest quarterly catastrophe bond market report shows . The Artemis Q3 2026 catastrophe bond and related insurance-linked securities (ILS) market report dissects an above-average $948 million issuance period for the sector following on from the record first-half. The Artemis Q3 2026 Catastrophe Bond Market Report, available to download now, examines cat bond and related insurance-linked securities (ILS) risk capital issued in the third-quarter of the year, key trends from the period and reviews nine month cat bond market activity .

item.title: European firms struggle to turn risk insight into action, Marsh finds
item.description: European organisations are taking steps to strengthen resilience but are struggling to translate risk insight into business action, according to new research from Marsh. Developed by Marsh’s European risk consulting practice and published ahead of FERMA Forum 2026 in Rotterdam, the survey examines how organisations are integrating risk management into decision-making across scenario planning, supply chain resilience, AI and analytics, workforce preparedness and infrastructure resilience. However, only around one-third use the findings against defined risk limits to confirm or adjust decisions, suggesting that risk analysis is not consistently feeding through into business decisions.

item.title: RVS Roundtable: Creativity and responsiveness key as reinsurance competition intensifies
item.description: Reinsurance industry leaders agreed that competitive pressure is a hallmark of current market conditions, but were eager to emphasise that some markets and products are still attractive amid all the talk of softening, with cedents looking for creativity, responsiveness, and transparency from their reinsurance partners. The full, comprehensive roundtable report will be released in the coming weeks, but in the meantime, below are some comments from representatives of our kind sponsors on reinsurance market conditions. At the 68th RVS conference in September, we hosted our fourth executive Monte Carlo Rendezvous roundtable, in partnership with SiriusPoint, BMS Group, and PwC.

item.title: Sompo appoints Scott Toland as Head of Commercial Lines, Insurance, Continental Europe
item.description: Sompo, a global provider of commercial and consumer property, casualty, and specialty re/insurance, has announced the appointment of Scott Toland as Head of Commercial Lines, Insurance, Continental Europe. In his new role, he will be responsible for defining and executing Sompo’s Commercial Lines underwriting strategy across Continental Europe. Brand commented, “Scott’s appointment marks an important step in the continued development of our Commercial Lines platform in Continental Europe.

item.title: Illinois Governor Creates Cabinet to Explore AI Regulation
item.description: The unpaid group, which will formulate policy proposals through 2027, will analyze and assess “the various risks posed by AI to the safety of Illinois residents and the critical infrastructure residents rely on.” It’s the latest move by Illinois to tackle state-focused AI regulation as the federal government continues to take a hands-off approach , even as industry insiders sound the alarm on the technology’s capabilities. The cabinet will formulate policies and procedures to protect Illinois residents and public assets like water systems, education and information systems from threats posed by AI. JB Pritzker is setting up a new group within state government to explore more regulations for artificial intelligence as calls grow across the country for new restrictions.

item.title: Wisconsin Manufacturer Settles Religious Accommodation Request
item.description: Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) to resolve for monetary and injunctive relief a religious accommodation charge involving an employee’s request to use biological pronouns for another employee, the federal agency announced. According to the EEOC’s reasonable cause finding, Generac violated Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 when it did not fully engage in the reasonable accommodation interactive process before denying a religious employee’s request to use biological sex-based pronouns when referring to a trans-identified employee, even after the religious employee informed Generac that using non-biological pronouns went against his sincerely held religious beliefs. Generac Power Systems, a Wisconsin generator manufacturer, reached an agreement with the U.S.

item.title: US Fund Accuses Radiant World of Fraud in Swiss Complaint
item.description: A US fund has filed a criminal complaint in Switzerland accusing Radiant World and related companies of fraud and money laundering, according to a US court filing, adding a new jurisdiction to the iron ore trader’s escalating legal and financial crisis. A spokesperson for the Swiss Federal Office of Justice, which acts as a clearinghouse for all foreign legal assistance queries, said it “has not received any request for legal assistance from Singapore or the United States in this matter.” Radiant World is facing a spate of civil lawsuits from Singapore to London over allegations from creditors that it provided banks with falsified documents to secure financing, while Singapore Police are also conducting an investigation into the company. In the US court papers, lawyers for Mariner said the firm entered into agreements with Radiant World under which it provided two revolving credit facilities totaling $50 million to finance certain metals trades.

item.title: Plymouth Rock welcomes AI insurance shoppers
item.description: Plymouth Rock is encouraging consumers to shop for home insurance through ChatGPT and Meta’s Muse, positioning AI as another entry point to its products alongside independent agents. The message follows Plymouth Rock’s July announcement introducing home insurance quoting within ChatGPT across its six operating states: Massachusetts, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Connecticut, New York and New Hampshire. “At Plymouth Rock, we’re not running from AI—we’re embracing it,” the company wrote on LinkedIn .

item.title: Hanwha Life plans $664 million Acuon acquisition
item.description: Hanwha Life and private equity firm Centroid Investment Partners are set to acquire Acuon Capital and Acuon Savings Bank in a package deal valued at nearly 900 billion won ($664 million), according to The Korea Economic Daily. Hanwha Life was selected as the preferred bidder approximately three months ago, beating Meritz Securities. The transaction involves acquiring a 96.06% stake in Acuon Capital from EQT.

item.title: Indigo surpasses $20 million in premiums
item.description: Indigo Risk Retention Group , the medical professional liability insurance platform, has surpassed $20 million in premiums, doubling its premium volume since announcing a $50 million Series B in January 2026. Indigo says roughly 40% of submissions now receive an automated underwriting decision, more than double last year’s rate. According to Indigo, this allows lower-risk physicians to receive pricing that reflects their risk profile rather than subsidizing higher-risk colleagues within a practice.

item.title: Allianz may be planning a second life reinsurance sidecar, Sconset Re II
item.description: Global insurance giant Allianz may be planning a new iteration of its Sconset Re life reinsurance sidecar vehicle, with new entities that align with that structures name having been pre-registered in Bermuda, sources have explained. Recall that, in late 2024 Allianz launched a Bermuda-domiciled life and annuity focused reinsurance sidecar named Sconset Re Ltd . Notably, in the second-quarter of 2026, Allianz said it received the first dividend payment from its investment participation in the Sconset Re sidecar, although no figure was disclosed for the amount earned.

item.title: Passengers Avert Crash Tackling Pilot Who Stabbed Colleague
item.description: A pilot of a jet carrying more than 170 passengers to Tel Aviv stabbed his colleague and tried to crash the plane in what Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu branded a serious security incident. Netanyahu said almost all of the passengers on the flight were Israelis, and that those who intervened “displayed exceptional resourcefulness and courage.” The airline said in a statement that “the underlying reasons and motives behind this event are unknown and remain subject to a formal investigation.” A repatriation flight sent to pick up the passengers has now landed in Tel Aviv with the passengers on board. Catastrophe was narrowly avoided after a passenger and members of crew stormed the cockpit of the Flydubai plane that had taken off in Dubai and managed to stabilize the jet, after it plunged more than 14,000 feet (4,300 meters) in less than 30 seconds at almost the speed of sound.

item.title: Liberty Mutual’s Certainly ends its last remaining product
item.description: Certainly , the digital insurance brand launched by Liberty Mutual in 2019, is no longer offering auto insurance. Bottom Line: Certainly’s roots trace back to Lulo, where Liberty Mutual tested whether it could replicate Lemonade’s $5 renters insurance pitch. Its website now directs shoppers to Liberty Mutual for a quote.

item.title: Flood Insurance vs. Home Insurance
item.description: In a recent report, Clearsurance.com explored the difference between home insurance and flood insurance. Insurance That Actually Covers Flooding If a flash flood happens in a homeowner’s region, standard home insurance will not cover flood damage. If a homeowner has a sump pump and it fails and the basement floods, neither standard home insurance nor flood insurance will cover the damage.

item.title: Plymouth Rock names Jared Stuckey VP of customer service and underwriting
item.description: Plymouth Rock has promoted Jared Stuckey to Vice President of Customer Service and Underwriting, effective immediately. Stuckey previously led underwriting strategy and managed personal and commercial products for Plymouth Rock’s independent agent auto business. Before joining Plymouth Rock, Stuckey spent 16 years at Liberty Mutual in senior product management and customer experience roles.

item.title: Zinnia Connects Life, Annuity Distribution Workflows
item.description: (Image credit: IIR.) Zinnia (Greenwich, Conn.) has launched a connected distribution experience within Zinnia Market Connect (ZMC), bringing multiple life and annuity sales functions into a single workflow for advisors. “Whether a firm wants to build on our APIs or use Zinnia Market Connect as their front end, we’re removing the friction that has shackled distribution for decades and replacing it with one connected system,” comments George Esposito, CEO, Zinnia. API-First Distribution Infrastructure Zinnia has also introduced Illustrations-as-a-Service, extending its composable approach beyond order entry into quoting and illustrations.

item.title: One Inc Launches XpressOne Vendor Payments
item.description: (Image credit: IIR.) One Inc (Folsom, Calif.) has launched XpressOne, a vendor-payment service designed to simplify how repair shops and other claims service providers receive and reconcile payments from insurers. XpressOne gives vendors a single place to manage payments across multiple carriers, locations and tax identification numbers (TIN). The service includes two payment options: XpressOne ClaimsCard, a card-based payment method, and XpressOne Direct, which sends funds directly to a vendor’s bank account.

item.title: India Caps Weakest Monsoon Since 2015, Raising Food Price Risks
item.description: A powerful El Niño has left India with its weakest monsoon in more than a decade, threatening crops, draining reservoirs and raising food-price risks in the world’s most populous nation. Rainfall during the June to September monsoon season was 12.6% below the long-term average, according to the India Meteorological Department. The shortfall was the worst since 2015, when precipitation was 12.7% below normal.

item.title: Bayer Faces Trial Test of Remaining Roundup Claims After Supreme Court Win
item.description: Attorneys for three cancer patients told a Missouri jury on Tuesday that Bayer’s Monsanto unit failed to adequately test its Roundup weedkiller before selling it, starting a trial that could help determine the viability of some Roundup lawsuits after a U.S. Related: Bayer Faces Test of $7.25B Roundup Settlement In Missouri Court Tuesday’s case before a different St. “To this day, they’ve never done all the testing they’ve needed to do.” Related: Bayer’s Supreme Court Win in Roundup Case No ‘Silver Bullet’ Bayer has denied the claims and said that decades of studies have shown glyphosate, Roundup’s active ingredient, is safe and does not cause cancer.

item.title: Rogue AI Agents Pose Uncertain Legal Risk for Anthropic
item.description: Anthropic could face legal claims from customers and users over the actions of rogue artificial intelligence agents, though the legal framework is uncertain, the company said in the prospectus for its stock market debut seen by Reuters. While it gears up for what could be the largest initial public offering ever, Anthropic faces the possibility of vast unknown legal risk if its agentic AI technology — designed to maintain deep access to customers’ systems and run autonomously for days at a time — goes rogue. A string of incidents involving rogue AI agents, from OpenAI’s autonomous agents hacking an AI startup and breaching an Australian health data portal, to several cybersecurity incidents involving Anthropic’s Claude AI models, has led to debate among researchers, investors and lawmakers over who is liable for harm from an autonomous AI system.

item.title: Men Sentenced in Multi-State Stolen Construction Equipment Scheme
item.description: The last of four defendants was sentenced this week in a multi-state theft ring that altered vehicle identification numbers on a variety of equipment used at construction sites, according to the U.S. The conspiracy involved tampering with Vehicle Identification Numbers (VINs), the use of a chop shop, fraudulent documentation, false business fronts and stolen identities to sell stolen equipment and further conceal their criminal activities An investigation of a shoplifting incident in the Juban Crossing Shopping Center led Livingston Parish Sheriff’s Office detectives to uncover an unregistered firearm silencer and 9mm pistol from a stolen pickup truck being operated by Byerley and King. Dennis Lloyd Sizemore, of Lafayette, Louisiana, was sentenced to 60 months in federal prison and Robert Gregory Brazell, also of Lafayette, Louisiana, was sentenced to 33 months in federal prison.

item.title: Hurricane Hunter Data Reveals 4 Signs of a Strengthening Storm
item.description: Nearly three decades of Hurricane Hunter data reveal four features that can help a tilted tropical cyclone straighten its circulation and become capable of intensifying. Scientists have identified four clues that could reveal when a tilted tropical cyclone is about to straighten up and become capable of rapidly strengthening, research by the University of Miami Rosenstiel School of Marine, Atmospheric, and Earth Science revealed. The findings could give forecasters an earlier warning that a seemingly disorganized storm is becoming primed to strengthen.

item.title: FCA announces new Board appointments
item.description: Three new appointments have been made to our Board, bringing additional experience in public policy, financial services, regulation and corporate leadership as we continue to deliver our strategy. Lea Paterson CBE and Matthew Tobin have been appointed by the Treasury as non-executive directors, while deputy chief executive Sarah Pritchard has joined the Board as an executive member. She is currently chair of the Senior Salaries Review Body, a Civil Service Commissioner and a board member of the Independent Parliamentary Standards Authority (IPSA).

item.title: Charter Space raises $5M to bring insurance to the stars
item.description: Charter Space, a finalist in last year’s TechCrunch Startup Battlefield , has raised a $5 million seed round to keep growing its budding space insurance business. As Charter explains on its website, a common experience for space companies is that regular insurers “heard a bunch of scary science words and freaked out.” When Chan started Charter Space with co-founder Yukun Yin, they set out to build a centralized software for aerospace engineering that would bring together the technical, manufacturing, and test data for customers. “Insurance is critical infrastructure for a strong and sustainable space industry, and we believe Charter Space is building the platform that will help the space economy scale safely and sustainably.” Michael Yaworsky, the commissioner of insurance regulation in Florida, still the leading launch location in the country, said insurance is “the precondition for growth in space” and said it opens the door for more local investment.

item.title: Stone Ridge cat bond fund hits $5bn AUM milestone, total mutual ILS assets now ~$7.6bn
item.description: The Stone Ridge High Yield Reinsurance Risk Premium Fund, the main catastrophe bond focused strategy operated by Stone Ridge, has reached a milestone of $5 billion in assets under management, while the investment manager’s AUM across its mutual catastrophe bond, insurance-linked securities and reinsurance funds now sits around $7.6 billion. At that roughly $7.6 billion level of total ILS related AUM in mutual funds, across the Stone Ridge High Yield Reinsurance Risk Premium Fund (the largest and most catastrophe bond focused strategy), the Stone Ridge Reinsurance Risk Premium Interval Fund, that invests across the spectrum of ILS and reinsurance-linked assets including sidecars and private quota shares, other collateralized reinsurance arrangements and to a lesser degree catastrophe bonds, and the cat bond and ILS component of the multi-strategy Stone Ridge Diversified Alternatives Fund, it has now increased by almost 30% in just one year. But, data seen by Artemis shows that Stone Ridge’s most cat bond focused investment fund grew again to around $4.9 billion by the end of August and as of this week stands just slightly under $5 billion (although may clear that milestone level in total net assets as soon as later today it seems).

item.title: Cyber insurers gain new visibility into AI exposure during underwriting: KYND
item.description: Cyber risk intelligence company KYND has introduced a new capability aimed at helping insurers identify artificial intelligence (AI) technologies across an organisation’s externally visible digital environment during the risk selection process. For insurers, understanding how AI is being deployed and what dependencies it creates can form part of assessing a cyber risk, although information about technology use is often based on what an organisation discloses during the underwriting process. “Giving underwriters independently observed information means the conversation can start with greater visibility of what is detectable on the risk, helping underwriters ask more informed questions and build a clearer picture of the exposure.” According to KYND, the new technology detection capability can identify a range of AI applications and features that are externally visible.

item.title: Handen to succeed van de Wall as Markel’s Head of Trade Credit & Political Risk, Americas
item.description: Markel Insurance, the insurance operation within Markel Group Inc., has announced the appointment of Jonathan Handen as Head of Trade Credit & Political Risk – Americas for its International operations. Based in Baltimore, Handen will report directly to Phil Amlot, Head of Trade Credit at Markel International, who commented: “While we speak to the Americas as a single region, its risk landscape is anything but homogenous, covering a vast range of geographies, industries and political networks. In his new position, Handen will oversee the Trade Credit and Political Risk portfolio across the Americas, driving underwriting performance, strategic growth and portfolio development across priority focus areas.

item.title: Property reinsurance rates expected to fall further in 2027, reveals Moody’s survey
item.description: Insurers expect property reinsurance prices to fall further in 2027, according to the latest reinsurance buyers survey from Moody’s Ratings, the credit rating agency. According to Moody’s, most respondents to its previous survey had correctly predicted that property reinsurance prices would fall in 2026, but generally underestimated how steep those declines would be. For property reinsurance, 86% of respondents to the 2026 survey expected prices to fall in the year ahead, up from 74% who said the same in the 2025 survey, pointing to a consensus around continued softening in the property market.

item.title: Bank of England Sees Growing Risk That Dangers From AI and Debt Will Materialize
item.description: The Bank of England on Wednesday warned of an increase in the risk that interconnected weaknesses in the financial system will crystallize, highlighting the re-escalation of the conflict in Iran and increased AI-related debt issuance. Read more : AI ‘Arms Race’ Still Poses Global Stability Risk, BIS Chief Says “The likelihood that interconnected vulnerabilities in the financial system crystallize has risen,” the FPC said in a record of its quarterly meeting. The “rapid increase” in AI-related debt issuance had also increased the exposure of capital markets to developments in AI, the FPC said.

item.title: Griffin’s University Plan Turbocharges Miami Transformation
item.description: With a $2 billion donation to build a Carnegie Mellon University campus in Miami’s Wynwood neighborhood, Griffin is betting that he can complete the transformation. Ken Griffin has spent years trying to reshape Miami from a playground for the world’s wealthy into a high-finance and technology hub. Griffin envisions the university as an educational incubator where engineering talent will be prepared to work at Citadel or to start businesses that will draw investment to South Florida for generations.

item.title: People Moves: Howden Re Launches Danish Office, Naming Ellborg as MD; Re/Insurance Broker Cogent Names Holberry as CEO Designate
item.description: This edition of International People Moves details appointments at Howden Re and the re/insurance broker Cogent. Howden Re Launches Danish Office, Naming Ellborg as MD Howden Re , the London-based reinsurance unit of Howden, has opened an office in Copenhagen and appointed Jens Ellborg as managing director, effective Nov. Ellborg will lead the expansion of Howden Re’s Danish offering, working closely with reinsurance colleagues across the region and with Howden Denmark.

item.title: The Dangers to Insurers From Reward Hacking
item.description: Such behavior is known as "reward hacking:" models pursuing the stated objective—capture the flag—through routes nobody intended or authorized. That's not fraud; it's reward hacking in a suit. AI agents optimizing for bind rates may exploit underwriting systems the same way OpenAI's test agents hacked shared infrastructure.

item.title: Fuse Launches Environmental Hub, Combining Safety, PFAS and Litigation Signals Into One View of the Waste Risk Market
item.description: The post Fuse Launches Environmental Hub, Combining Safety, PFAS and Litigation Signals Into One View of the Waste Risk Market appeared first on Coverager - Insurance news and insights . It brings together rate & rule filings, regulatory actions & pfas, litigation & verdict trends, fleet & workplace safety, and carrier appetite shifts, and turns them into a synthesized view of market direction. Fuse synthesizes rate filings, statutory financials, litigation trends, cost data, peril activity, and capital and reinsurance signals into market intelligence by vertical and state for brokers, carriers and reinsurers.

item.title: MSI expands embedded insurance to manufactured housing
item.description: MSI , the MGA owned by The Baldwin Group, has extended its embedded insurance platform to manufactured home communities. MSI says the US has nearly eight million manufactured homes housing more than 16 million people. Available nationwide, the offering combines insurance coverage options with automated compliance tracking through LeaseTrack.

item.title: Kin opens its doors to AI shopping agents
item.description: Kin announced that consumers using Meta’s Muse and other AI agents can shop for home insurance quotes through Kin.com, positioning the approach as an alternative to insurers and marketplaces that block automated shopping. Harper argued that AI shopping agents could challenge distribution models built around brokers and independent agents. Kin expects AI agents to handle more of the work involved in shopping for insurance, including gathering information, entering it across websites, comparing coverage and explaining options.

item.title: PuntoSeguro permite comparar seguros de Vida desde ChatGPT
item.description: PuntoSeguro ha lanzado una aplicación en ChatGPT que permite comparar seguros de Vida de 10 aseguradoras dentro de una conversación. La correduría la presenta como el primer comparador de este tipo disponible en ChatGPT en España. OpenAI ha revisado y aprobado la aplicación para publicarla en la plataforma.

item.title: Carlos Olave, nuevo director de Personas y Comunicación de SegurCaixa Adeslas
item.description: SegurCaixa Adeslas ha incorporado a Carlos Olave como nuevo director de Personas y Comunicación, con responsabilidad sobre ambas áreas en el marco de la estrategia de crecimiento y transformación de la compañía.
